original_value: AbstractRecently, human gait pattern has turned into an essential biometric feature to recognize an individual remotely. Gait as a feature becomes challenging owing to variation in appearance under different covariate conditions (eg, shoe, surface, haul, viewpoint and attire). The covariates may alter few fragment of gait while other fragment stay unaltered, leading to lower the probability of correct identification. To overcome such variation, an improved gait recognition strategy is proposed in this article by gait energy image partitioning and selection processing. Our method involves pre‐processing of raw video for silhouette extraction, gait cycle detection, segmentation into different regions, and histogram of gradients feature extraction from selected segments. In this way, the specific features across complete gait cycles are extracted precisely. Finally, recognition is done by using K‐NN. The proposed strategy has been assessed using the CASIA B gait database. Our outcomes shows a particular proposed strategy accomplishes high recognition rate and outperforms the advanced gait recognition mechanism.

result.paraphrase: Abstract Human gait patterns have become an important biometric trait for remotely identifying individuals. However, gait recognition is difficult because appearance changes under covariates such as shoes, walking surface, load, viewpoint, and clothing. These covariates can alter some parts of the gait while leaving others unchanged, which reduces the chance of correct identification. To address this variability, this article proposes an improved gait recognition approach based on gait energy image partitioning and selection processing. The method preprocesses raw video to extract silhouettes, detect gait cycles, divide them into different regions, and extract histogram of gradients features from the selected segments. This allows specific features across full gait cycles to be captured accurately. Recognition is then performed using K-NN. The proposed strategy was evaluated on the CASIA B gait database, and the results show that it achieves a high recognition rate and outperforms the advanced gait recognition mechanism.
